an_arm_of_my_own_design_that_cannot_diff.why_that_is_correct_and_not_a_bug: `no_autocast` exists to stop upstream downcasting a FLOAT64 graph: it neutralises `torch.amp.autocast` and makes `Tensor.float()` identity ONLY on float64 tensors. At float32 there is nothing to protect -- autocast(float32) is a no-op and .float() is already identity -- so arm3 is the same computation as arm2 by construction.
an_arm_of_my_own_design_that_cannot_diff.whose_error: mine. I specified the arm3 - arm2 contrast in the brief and pre-registered it as isolating 'upstream's own casting from single precision itself'. It cannot differ at fp32, so it isolates nothing. Same family as the power-of-two scale-invariance arm: a contrast built so that it cannot move.
an_arm_of_my_own_design_that_cannot_diff.what_would_actually_isolate_it: the comparison must be at a dtype where upstream's casts bite -- i.e. the bf16 arm with and without no_autocast, not the fp32 pair.
